patterns.name: Specification triple: API / reference implementation / TCK as sibling projects
patterns.description: Each OSGi specification is realized as up to three sibling bnd projects: org.osgi.service.<spec> (API bundle), org.osgi.impl.service.<spec> (reference implementation), org.osgi.test.cases.<spec> (TCK). The TCK's -runbundles wires the RI under test; some RIs ship as prebuilt binaries in licensed/repo instead of source projects (e.g. event impl).
rules: API project exports exactly the spec packages; impl project is fully private (-privatepackage ${p}.*)
Impl bundle declares Export-Service and registers via Bundle-Activator
TCK project names impl under test in -runbundles with version=latest
Directory name == BSN for all three projects
patterns.graphCommunities: TCK/impl/API triads dominate the 905 Leiden communities; hub DefaultTestBundleControl (321 edges) confirms TCK support coupling

patterns.name: Central cnf/build.bnd + composable cnf/includes/*.bnd layers
patterns.description: All cross-cutting build config lives in cnf/build.bnd (global headers, version scheme, signing/packaging plugins, -runfw). Per-project bnd.bnd files start with -include: ${includes}/jdt.bnd plus a layer file (core.bnd, cmpn.bnd, tck.bnd, promise.bnd, companion.bnd) selecting the API level, keeping project files 8-30 lines.
rules: Global identity headers (Bundle-Vendor, Bundle-SCM, Bundle-License, Git-SHA) stamped once in cnf/build.bnd
Per-project bnd.bnd first line: -include: ${includes}/jdt.bnd, ${includes}/<layer>.bnd
Reproducible builds: -reproducible: true, -noextraheaders: true, LICENSE+NOTICE embedded via -includeresource.legal
-diffignore: Bundle-Version so baselining ignores timestamp versions

patterns.name: Package-level semantic versioning via @Version package-info.java
patterns.description: Every exported package carries a package-info.java with @Version("x.y") from org.osgi.annotation.versioning; javadoc documents distinct consumer [1.5,2.0) vs provider [1.5,1.6) import ranges. Bundle versions are build-timestamped and excluded from baselining; the package version is the semantic contract.
rules: package-info.java: @Version("major.minor") — never micro in the annotation
Javadoc states consumer and provider Import-Package range examples
Export-Package: ${p}.*; -split-package:=first in API bnd.bnd
Baselining ignores Bundle-Version (-diffignore), package versions gate compatibility

patterns.name: TCK tests execute inside the reference framework with embedded test bundles
patterns.description: TCK projects run JUnit tests in-framework (-runfw org.osgi.impl.framework). Test classes extend org.osgi.test.support.OSGiTestCase which receives the BundleContext from the OSGi JUnit runner (FrameworkUtil fallback). Scenario bundles tb1.jar/tb2.jar are built on demand by the -make recipe from bnd/tbN.bnd and embedded as resources; -signaturetest asserts API signature fidelity.
rules: -conditionalpackage = org.osgi.test.support.* copies support classes into the TCK bundle
-privatepackage = ${p}.junit holds tests; Export-Package = ${p}.service holds shared test API
-includeresource = tb1.jar, tb2.jar + bnd/tbN.bnd recipes (-make (*).(jar);type=bnd;recipe="bnd/$1.bnd")
-signaturetest = <api package> for signature verification
Security variant lives in a sibling *.secure project, not a flag
patterns.graphCommunities: DefaultTestBundleControl (321 edges) and BundleContext (1699) god nodes anchor the TCK communities

patterns.name: Reference implementation registers spec service via BundleActivator (+ServiceFactory)
patterns.description: RI bundles declare Bundle-Activator in bnd.bnd and Export-Service metadata. The activator registers the spec service, often implementing ServiceFactory so each consuming bundle gets a scoped instance; all impl packages stay private.
rules: Bundle-Activator = ${p}.Activator (package == BSN)
Export-Service: <spec service FQN> declared in bnd.bnd
-privatepackage = ${p}.* — implementation never exports packages
-buildpath: spec API project version=latest + org.osgi.framework maven-scope=provided

patterns.name: Single bnd-workspace Gradle build over ~190 BSN-named projects
patterns.description: settings.gradle applies biz.aQute.bnd.workspace; gradle.properties pins bnd_version and seeds the project graph from bnd_build=osgi.build so Gradle builds exactly the bnd workspace dependency closure. No per-project build.gradle logic needed for standard bundles.
rules: bnd workspace plugin version pinned once (bnd_version=7.1.0)
Workspace properties injected via gradle.ext.bndWorkspaceConfigure
Aggregate projects (osgi.core, osgi.cmpn, osgi.tck) assemble deliverables from -make/-includeresource, not Gradle logic
-workingset filters partition projects into Build/Companion/Implementations/TCKs views
